critique.cause: רוחב כולל של 573 פיקסלים נובע בעיקר מהקצאת 123 למחיר ו-180 להערות, נוסף על 107 לשכונה ו-100 לקומה.

critique.good: שכונה, מחיר וחדרים נראים בתחילת התצוגה, כל הכותרות שלמות ואין פיצול מילים. מחיר ויחידת הזמן נפרדים לשורות באופן שעדיין מאפשר להשוות מחירים.
critique.problems: הקומה נפרסת למספר שורות צרות, וההערות ארוכות מאוד לגובה; הדבר מרחיק בין דירות ומשאיר חללים גדולים בעמודות המספריות. רוב ההערות עדיין מחייב גלילה אופקית.
critique.cause: 63 פיקסלים לקומה ו-100 להערות משאירים רק 42 ו-79 פיקסלים לטקסט בהתאמה; רוחב הטקסט בהערות מגיע בדיוק לאורך המילה הארוכה ביותר.

understanding.purpose: להשוות בין דירות להשכרה בתל אביב לפי שכונה, מחיר, מספר חדרים, קומה והערות.
understanding.reading: הקוראים סורקים מימין לשמאל כדי לזהות שכונה, להשוות מחיר וחדרים, ואז לבדוק קומה והערות לכל דירה. גובה שורה שנוצר מהערה ארוכה יכול להכיל גם גלישה טבעית בתאים אחרים באותה שורה.
groups: שכונה מזהה כל דירה ומשמשת עוגן לקריאת השורה.
מחיר וחדרים הם נתונים עיקריים להשוואה וצריכים להיות קלים לסריקה יחד.
קומה והערות מספקות פרטים משלימים שעשויים להשפיע על הבחירה.
keep_intact: שמות השכונות ומילים בודדות ככל האפשר
מספרי מחירים, מספרי חדרים ומספרי קומות

bad.why: The floor column breaks short floor and elevator descriptions into as many as five lines, while the narrow notes column makes the table exceptionally tall. The modest reduction in horizontal scrolling comes at a substantial cost to row scanning.

final.rationale: r3A keeps neighborhood names on one line and the floor descriptions in compact phrases, so the four comparison columns read clearly together in the initial viewport. Its wider notes column gives the long prose a more comfortable measure and reduces the large empty areas alongside it. Reading the notes requires a substantial horizontal scroll, but the notes are secondary to the initial comparison.

general: Give identifying and frequently compared fields enough width to remain easy to scan together.
Allocate width according to content and role; long prose benefits from more width than short numeric fields.
Judge horizontal scrolling against the vertical fragmentation and row height caused by squeezing.
specific: The notes contain much more text than the other columns and largely determine row height.
At 107px, the neighborhood column accommodates the longest full name on one line; the narrower versions wrap some row labels.
The four principal columns in r3A occupy 353px, leaving the notes mostly beyond the initial 360px viewport.

final.tradeoffs: r3C makes the rows notably shorter and the notes easier to read, at the cost of 46px more horizontal overflow than r3A. r2C reduces scrolling but wraps some neighborhood names and floor descriptions more heavily.
final.uncertain: A designer who expects readers to consult notes for every listing might prefer r3C; one prioritizing less horizontal scrolling might accept r2C. The ranges are approximate visual tolerances, not browser-verified breakpoints, and assume the other columns remain near their preferred proportions.

A.why: Neighborhoods and prices are easy to scan, but floor descriptions break into several short lines and the notes require horizontal scrolling.

B.why: The main comparison columns fit at first sight, and floor descriptions usually stay on two lines. The notes sit beyond the viewport and make rows tall.

C.why: Neighborhood, price, rooms and floor are readable together, with floor descriptions on two lines. The wider notes appear to reduce row height, though they require horizontal scrolling.

D.why: The table fits the viewport, but neighborhood names and many words in the notes split across lines. Extremely tall rows make comparisons difficult.

E.why: The main comparison columns fit at first sight and row heights are moderate. Some floor descriptions take three lines, and the notes require horizontal scrolling.

F.why: All columns are near the viewport, but narrow notes create very tall rows, floor descriptions fragment, and some neighborhood names and prices wrap awkwardly.

reviews.unsure: The left portions of the scrolling layouts are outside the supplied image view, so the full notes widths and exact scrolling distances cannot be judged directly.

A.why: All columns fit, but the notes and several neighborhood names break within words. The narrow notes column makes the rows extremely tall and difficult to scan.

B.why: Neighborhoods, prices and room counts are easy to compare, but floor details wrap into many short lines and the notes require horizontal scrolling.

C.why: The first four columns read clearly, with floor details grouped into two lines. Notes lie almost entirely beyond the viewport, so reading them requires scrolling.

D.why: The main comparison columns are clear and the rows are shorter than in C. Some floor details take three lines, and the notes require horizontal scrolling.

E.why: Nearly the whole table is visible, but notes are set in a very narrow measure, prices separate from their currency symbols, and floor details fragment into short lines.

F.why: Neighborhoods, prices, rooms and floor details are clear and compact, with floor descriptions generally held to two lines. The notes require horizontal scrolling.

reviews.unsure: The supplied views do not show the full notes columns in the scrolling layouts, so their line breaks and the total scrolling distance are difficult to assess.
